explanatory_strength.rationale: The contract explains the economic claim correctly and in the right units. It resists the two errors this asset class invites: it applies the Company's OpCo economic interest before the per-share division so the Continuing Equity Owners' 14.0% is never counted as Class A value, and it refuses to subtract net debt and the mezzanine preferred from a CAFD-derived value when CAFD is already struck after cash interest and cash preferred dividends. The partition of the 206,473 MMcfe proved book into 178,544 MMcfe producing and 27,930 MMcfe non-producing is the correct way to pair an owner-cash leg with a unit-NAV leg without valuing the same molecules twice. It loses a point because the whole structure is a perpetuity approximation of a finite book rather than a period-by-period distribution curve.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Every number traces to the 424B4 and the CG&A reserve report, which is the right tier of evidence, but there is only one filing generation of it. No 10-Q or 10-K has been filed since the 2026-06-10 IPO, so nothing in the packet can be diffed against a prior period, and the reserve report has never been re-cut. The frozen adversarial review performed no filing reconciliation and the third-party cross-check indexes zero sources. Most decisive for my lens: the unbooked mineral acreage is nowhere quantified, and for a fee mineral owner that is not a rounding item.

downside_control.rationale: There is no contractual floor under this security. The distribution is undeclared, the reserves deplete on a 7.27-year producing life, and royalty revenue is an unhedged pass-through of gas price and operator drilling decisions with no operating lever available to management. The $30.643m Series B preferred sits ahead of Class A. The one genuine support is that the assets are real, saleable minerals held in fee rather than a lease that expires, which is why this is a 2 and not a 1.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: At $26.16 against a base of $5.71 the contract computes a negative 19.53% annualised return over seven years, and the high case is still negative 17.45%. Class A market capitalisation of roughly $602m plus $64.5m net debt and $30.6m preferred against a PV-10 of $293.690m is about 2.7x PV-10. Mineral companies do trade above PV-10 because the SEC deck is backward-looking and proved-only, but 2.7x with an 8.4-year proved life and no declared dividend is not a scarce-asset entry point.

votes.strongest_counter_explanation: WhiteHawk owns minerals in fee across the Marcellus and Haynesville, so its economic life is not the 8.4-year proved reserve life - it is however long premier operators such as EQT, Antero, Range and CNX keep drilling the acreage, which on Appalachian inventory is measured in decades. Proved reserves are a booking convention constrained by SEC rules and the five-year PUD window, not an inventory census. On that reading the correct model is a perpetual royalty on a drilling program, the observed pro forma volume change of only -4.4% (67,255 to 64,270 Mcfe/d) is the true net decline rather than the -13.75% PDP decline, and the market's roughly 2.7x PV-10 is the normal multiple for a mineral company with long unbooked inventory rather than an overvaluation. If that is right, this contract's base is too low by a wide margin and the error is mine, not the market's.
votes.most_important_missing_fact: A quantification of unbooked mineral inventory - net royalty acres by play with undrilled location counts and operator permit or rig activity against them - so the volume beyond the 206,473 MMcfe proved book can be risked and valued instead of left at zero.
falsifiers: The first 10-Q reports net production above 67,255 Mcfe/d, which would mean the producing decline is shallower than the 13.14% to 13.75% band the reserve report implies and the owner-cash component is understated.
The FY2026 reserve report raises PV-10 above $500m, i.e. above $0.00242m per MMcfe on the current book, resetting the unit value both components rest on.
Operator permit and rig data on WhiteHawk's acreage shows a drilling program large enough to sustain volumes flat for a decade, which would falsify the finite-life framing entirely.
specialist_findings: The scarce-asset lens requires non-overlapping physical inventory, and the packet now supplies it: the two components partition the proved book with no volume counted twice and the contract reports no double_counting_flags.
PV-10 is a 10% pre-tax discounting under SEC rules, and the owner-cash component's base required return is also 10%, so the two legs are discount-rate comparable rather than accidentally divergent.

The tax bridge is handled properly for once: the $27.364m difference between PV-10 of $293.690m and the standardized measure of $266.326m is applied as a 9.32% drag on the NAV component rather than ignored.

The realization haircut of 0.40/0.55/0.70 on non-producing volumes is the weakest judgment in the NAV leg. It is a timing proxy standing in for a proper schedule of when those 27,930 MMcfe come online, and no filed document supports the specific band.

explanatory_strength.rationale: The asset claim is stated plainly and the bridge from asset to Class A share is complete: 206,473 MMcfe of proved reserves, a PV-10 of $293.690m and a standardized measure of $266.326m, an 86.0% OpCo economic interest falling to 82.1% if the earnout units issue, 22,996,579 Class A shares, and $95.106m of senior claims. Nothing material is left implicit. The one structural weakness is that neither component deducts capitalised corporate overhead from asset value, which for a royalty vehicle with pro forma G&A of $27.4m is not nothing.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: For an asset-value determination the evidence is adequate. A third-party engineering firm, CG&A, prepared the reserve report; PV-10 and the standardized measure are SEC-defined computations, not management estimates; and reserve quantities, share counts and the capital structure all come off the 424B4. That is enough to establish what the assets are worth today. It is not a 4 or 5 because the accounting that produces the cash figures was restated on April 22, 2026, seven weeks before the offering, with identified material weaknesses in internal control over the exact lines - management-fee recording and acquisition cash classification - that this story runs through, and no post-IPO filing exists to confirm remediation.

downside_control.rationale: Margin of safety is not merely absent, it is inverted. The purchase price is roughly 4.6x the contract's base asset value and 3.8x even the high case. Class A market capitalisation of about $602m plus $64.5m of net debt and $30.6m of preferred is roughly 2.7x a PV-10 of $293.690m, and PV-10 is a pre-tax figure - against the after-tax standardized measure of $266.326m the multiple is worse. The asset itself depletes on an 8.4-year proved life, so time works against the holder rather than for them. There is no declared distribution to be paid while waiting.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Negative 19.53% annualised on the base and negative 21.37% on the low case. Even the high case, which assumes the earnout never dilutes, a 9% required return and the shallowest decline the reserve report permits, returns negative 17.45%. There is no case in the contract in which this is a positive-return holding at $26.16, and the 15% base hurdle entry price is $2.15. Any liquid alternative dominates this.

votes.strongest_counter_explanation: PV-10 is a deliberately conservative construct and a poor proxy for what minerals actually change hands at. It is struck at a trailing twelve-month average deck of $3.387/MMBtu Henry Hub, uses a fixed 10% discount rate regardless of asset quality, and by rule counts only proved reserves - excluding all undrilled locations on fee acreage that never expires. Marcellus and Haynesville mineral packages transact well above PV-10 for exactly those reasons, and WhiteHawk's operators are the best-capitalised in the basin. On that view my 2.7x multiple is measuring the conservatism of the SEC convention rather than any overvaluation, and rejecting on it would be mistaking an accounting floor for intrinsic value.
votes.most_important_missing_fact: A set of arms-length transaction comparables for Marcellus and Haynesville mineral and royalty packages expressed as a multiple of PV-10 and as dollars per net royalty acre, which would establish whether 2.7x PV-10 is a normal clearing price for this asset class or a genuine premium.
falsifiers: Transaction comparables showing Appalachian mineral packages clearing consistently above 2.5x PV-10, which would mean the market price is within the normal range for the asset class and this rejection is anchored on an accounting convention.

A declared dividend at an annualised Class A rate above $1.30 per share that is sustained through a full reserve-report cycle, which would falsify the claim that CAFD cannot support a real distribution.
The FY2026 reserve report raising PV-10 above $500m, which would cut the price-to-asset-value multiple by more than 40% without any change in the share price.
specialist_findings: The liquidation-style bridge is clean: gross reserve value, less the SEC-computed future tax drag of $27.364m, less senior claims, at the Company's economic interest, over Class A shares. No step is skipped and no claim is netted twice.

Using the pre-tax PV-10 as the unit-value anchor rather than the after-tax standardized measure is the more generous of the two available choices, and the contract still cannot reach a positive return. The conclusion is robust to that choice.
The earnout is treated correctly and conservatively: low and base assume the 1,250,000 OpCo units issue and dilute the Company to 82.1%, with only the high case retaining 86.0%.

Corporate overhead is the one real omission. Capitalising even $8m per year of recurring cash G&A over the 8.4-year proved life at 10% would remove roughly $44m of value, about $1.57 per Class A share at the 82.1% interest - which would push the base below $4.20 and make this rejection stronger, not weaker.

explanatory_strength.rationale: The capital structure is laid out and the seniority ordering is respected: $75.0m of debt against $10.537m of cash, a $30.643m Series B preferred in mezzanine ranking ahead of Class A, and Series D fully redeemed with IPO proceeds. The contract also correctly refuses to deduct those claims twice, since CAFD is struck after cash interest and cash preferred dividends. What it does not do is model the cycle at all. Both components hold the $3.387/MMBtu SEC deck fixed across low, base and high, so the single variable that determines whether this credit is money-good never moves.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Nothing in this packet has survived a reporting cycle. No 10-Q or 10-K exists since the 2026-06-10 IPO, sec_companyfacts carries only S-1 fee-table concepts, and every operating figure is pro forma. The covenants governing the Senior Notes and the Revolving Credit Facility are referenced in the prospectus as restricting dividends but their terms, tests and headroom are not in the packet. The frozen adversarial review is a mechanical batch pass that reconciled no filings and scanned no disclosures, and the third-party cross-check indexes no sources. For a credit judgement that is not enough.

downside_control.rationale: Leverage is genuinely modest - $64.5m of net debt against $64.405m of pro forma Adjusted EBITDA is about 1.0x, which is why this is not a 1. But the protection is thinner than that ratio suggests. Adjusted EBITDA is struck after adding back $21.795m of management fees and $11.596m of transaction costs; pro forma operating cash flow was $9.533m and pro forma Q1 2026 operating cash flow was negative $10.714m. Against a proved book that depletes on an 8.4-year life, leverage rises mechanically every year unless acquisitions replace it, and acquisitions are exactly what a tighter credit market removes.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Negative 19.53% annualised on the base with no positive case anywhere in the range. The cycle framing makes it worse rather than better: the entity is being priced at roughly 2.7x PV-10 on a deck of $3.387/MMBtu that is already well above the $2.13 deck of the prior reserve report, so the multiple is being paid on top of an already-recovered price. That is the configuration in which capital-cycle losses are made, not avoided.

votes.strongest_counter_explanation: This is a royalty, not an operator, and that changes the credit picture materially. WhiteHawk funds no drilling capital, bears no lease operating expense and carries no plugging and abandonment liability, so its cost structure cannot be squeezed by service inflation and it has no maintenance capex obligation that a downturn makes unaffordable. At 1.0x leverage with those characteristics the credit is genuinely defensive, and a gas price decline reduces cash flow without threatening solvency. Under that reading the cyclical concern belongs in the discount rate, which the contract already sets at 9% to 12%, and pricing it a second time through the vote is double-counting the same risk.
votes.most_important_missing_fact: The covenant terms of the Senior Notes and the Revolving Credit Facility - the leverage and coverage tests, the restricted-payment basket governing dividends, and current headroom - which determine whether a gas price decline forces a distribution cut before it threatens anything else.
falsifiers: A covenant schedule showing a restricted-payment basket and leverage headroom wide enough to sustain distributions through a $2.13/MMBtu deck, which would materially reduce the credit risk I am pricing.
The first 10-Q showing actual operating cash flow converging toward the CAFD run-rate rather than the $9.533m pro forma FY2025 figure, which would mean the add-backs are genuinely non-recurring.

A demonstrated acquisition track record replacing reserves at accretive prices through a full gas cycle rather than the twelve-month PHX and TRR window, which would falsify the mechanical-releveraging concern.
specialist_findings: Both components hold the SEC price deck fixed across all three cases, so the range measures uncertainty in decline, discount rate and ownership but not in the commodity price - which for an unhedged royalty is the dominant variable. The stated range is therefore narrower than the true distribution.

The prior reserve report's $2.13/MMBtu deck produced $72.153m of PV-10 on 87,213 MMcfe, or $0.827 per Mcfe, against $1.422 per Mcfe at $3.387. A 59% price move produced a 72% move in value per unit; that elasticity is the missing sensitivity.

The pro forma preferred dividend deduction of $7.076m equals the historical FY2025 figure exactly and appears not to have been adjusted for the Series D redemption completed with IPO proceeds, which makes pro forma CAFD conservative on that one line by roughly $4m to $5m.

The earnout is struck on Adjusted EBITDA targets that the company itself defines and reports, on a measure that already carries $21.8m of fee add-backs. That is a governance exposure sitting on the same non-GAAP measure the credit is judged by.

pre_mortem.failure_story: Capital is committed near $26 on the strength of a $36.3m pro forma Cash Available for Distribution figure read as a durable income stream. It is not one. CAFD is struck before depletion: pro forma DD&A of $36.451m is essentially equal to pro forma CAFD of $36.317m, and pro forma FY2025 net income is a $32.330m loss. The reserve report behind it books 206,473 MMcfe against 24,548 MMcfe of pro forma annual production - an 8.4-year total proved life and a 7.27-year producing life. Distributions are therefore mostly return of capital on a wasting asset. Gas prices soften back toward the $2.13/MMBtu deck that produced the prior year's $72m PV-10 rather than the $3.387 deck behind today's $293.690m. The board, having never declared a dividend as a public company, sets an initial payout below what the CAFD headline implied, or cuts it within two years as PDP rolls over. The equity re-rates from roughly 2.7x PV-10 toward asset value. Holders discover late that the FY2025 restatement concluded seven weeks before the IPO and the identified material weaknesses in internal control were not cosmetic: the misstatements were in management-fee recording and acquisition cash classification, the two lines that the Internalization and the acquisition-driven growth story both run through. The earnout, up to 1,250,000 additional OpCo units against Adjusted EBITDA targets the company itself defines and reports, is met on reported numbers while per-share value falls.
earliest_warnings: The first 10-Q as a public company reports net production below the 64,270 Mcfe/d run-rate of Q1 2026 without an offsetting acquisition, confirming the producing decline is real and unmitigated.
An initial declared dividend materially below the pro forma CAFD run-rate of roughly $1.30 per Class A share, or a stated policy of retaining CAFD for acquisitions instead of distributing it.
Any restatement, late filing, or repeat material-weakness disclosure in the first 10-Q or 10-K, given the April 22, 2026 conclusion that FY2025 statements could not be relied upon.
Adjusted EBITDA outperformance concentrated in periods that determine the earnout, with the gain traceable to acquisition timing or fee add-backs rather than volumes.
The FY2026 reserve report showing negative revisions to the 206,473 MMcfe proved book, or PV-10 falling toward the prior-year $72m level on a lower SEC price deck.
forensic_checks: Reconcile CAFD to net cash provided by operating activities line by line. Pro forma FY2025 operating cash flow is $9.533m against $36.317m of CAFD, and pro forma Q1 2026 operating cash flow is negative $10.714m against $9.959m of CAFD. Confirm which add-backs are genuinely non-recurring rather than recharacterised operating costs.

Test the management-fee add-back of $21.795m. It comprises $6.2m Base Management Fees, $3.7m Dividend Incentive Fees and $13.6m Liquidity Incentive Fees less $1.7m of estimated internal compensation. The Liquidity Incentive Fee is IPO-triggered and would never recur; confirm the run-rate saving is the roughly $8.2m of recurring fees replaced by internal cost, not the headline $21.8m.
Compare depletion to CAFD every period. If DD&A continues to approximate CAFD, the distribution is return of capital and the payout ratio on economic earnings exceeds 100%.

Recompute PV-10 sensitivity to the SEC price deck. The FY2024 column shows $72.153m of PV-10 on 87,213 MMcfe at $2.13/MMBtu Henry Hub against $293.690m on 206,473 MMcfe at $3.387; isolate how much of the year-over-year gain is price rather than the PHX and TRR acquisitions.

Trace the Up-C ownership arithmetic. The prospectus states IPO purchasers hold 24.8% of OpCo indirectly, while 33.5% of the Company times the Company's 86.0% OpCo interest is 28.8%. Those do not tie; establish which is right before relying on any per-share figure.
Read the restatement disclosure and the remediation plan in full, and confirm whether the auditor has opined on internal control over financial reporting or is exempt as a newly public company.

responses.answer: The packet cannot answer this. No artifact in the frozen snapshot carries net mineral acres, average royalty rate, undrilled location counts, or operator permit and rig activity. The contract states the position rather than resolving it: the NAV component's assumption_summary records 'Booked non-producing reserves only; unbooked acreage is deliberately uncredited', and the producing component's pdp_decline rationale notes that any decline shallower than the band would reach 'into unbooked acreage that no filed reserve report supports'. The only adjacent datum is directional, not quantitative: pro forma net production fell 4.4% year over year (67,255 to 64,270 Mcfe/d) while the producing reserve book implies a 13.14% to 13.75% decline, so roughly 9 percentage points of annual volume is already being replaced by new wells converting inventory. That is evidence that unbooked inventory exists and is being drilled; it is not a measurement of how much remains.
responses.impact_if_resolved: This is the single largest unpriced variable in the contract. It is the most plausible explanation for the gap between the $5.71 base and the $26.16 market price, and hk's vote is explicitly conditioned on it.

responses.answer: The packet establishes the instruments and their recently amended economics but not a single covenant test. Resolved from the frozen deep dive and valuation.json: pro forma total debt is $75.0m of Senior Notes with the Revolving Credit Facility undrawn ($0) both actual and as-adjusted; the RCF was amended 2026-06-10 with Capital One, National Association as administrative agent; the Note Purchase Agreement was amended 2026-06-09, the issuer changed to WhiteHawk Income Operating Partnership L.P., the rate was cut from Adjusted Term SOFR + 6.50% to + 4.75%, and maturity extended from 2030-06-23 to 2031-05-20. Actual debt before the offering was $231.425m, so the IPO deleveraged materially. One further item bears directly on the contract: the capitalization footnote records that the as-adjusted $75.0m does not reflect a voluntary $6.3m Senior Notes prepayment made in April 2026, so debt at IPO close may be nearer $68.7m. Unresolved: no leverage test, no coverage test, no restricted-payment basket, and no headroom calculation appears anywhere in the packet. The rate reduction and maturity extension are indirect evidence that lenders viewed the credit as improving, but they are not a covenant schedule.
responses.impact_if_resolved: Determines whether a gas price decline forces a distribution cut before it threatens anything else. Separately, the unreflected $6.3m prepayment means the contract's $95.106m senior_claims fact may overstate the true claim by that amount; correcting it would raise the NAV bridge by roughly $0.23 per Class A share at the 82.1% interest, which does not change any vote.

research_loop.summary: Of three decision-material questions the packet resolves one partially and neither of the other two. The instruments and pricing of the debt are known and recently improved, but no covenant test is available. Unbooked acreage - the variable that would most change the answer - is not quantified anywhere, and the packet contains no third-party or comparable-transaction evidence at all. Two of the three insufficient-evidence findings therefore stand unresolved into round two, and the one new fact surfaced (the unreflected $6.3m April 2026 prepayment) is favourable but immaterial at roughly $0.23 per share.

That confirms unbooked inventory exists and is being drilled. It does not size what remains, so my position is unchanged.

PV-10 is a conservative construct: a trailing-twelve-month deck of $3.387/MMBtu, a fixed 10% discount rate regardless of asset quality, and proved reserves only, excluding every undrilled location on fee acreage that never expires. Appalachian mineral packages transact above PV-10 for exactly those reasons and WhiteHawk's operators are the best-capitalised in the basin. If 2.5x to 3.0x PV-10 is where this asset class actually clears, then my multiple is measuring the conservatism of an accounting convention and I am mistaking a floor for intrinsic value. The research loop could not test this, so it stands as the strongest argument against my vote.
